standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equivalence between the defining completed normal form and the delta-invariant equal to branches minus one.

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Example example-glue-points and Lemma lemma-factor-almost-isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Defines the glueing operation and factors the normalization map into glueings and tangent-vector squishings.

core_obligations: (3) implies (2) (proof lines 3494-3513): descending induction shows all U_i have multicross singularities; at a glueing point c the completed local ring embeds into the product of the two completed rings with equal residues, so branches add and the delta-invariant adds plus 1 (the inclusion has codimension 1), verifying branches - 1 = delta.

(1) and (2) imply (3) (proof lines 3515-3530): take U with x its only singular point and factor the normalization by lemma-factor-almost-isomorphism; a smallest squishing step would preserve the number of branches while raising delta by 1, contradicting the multicross-algebra characterization, so every step is a glueing.
proof_roadmap: Import the algebraic equivalence of the normal form and the delta-invariant count.
Run descending induction over a glueing tower, computing branches and delta at each glued point via the completed-ring inclusion.
Factor the normalization of a one-singularity neighbourhood by the almost-isomorphism lemma.
Exclude the squishing step by the branch-preserving delta-raising computation and conclude all steps are glueings.

The proof (lines 3492-3530) is complete: the algebraic equivalence is imported, the forward direction runs a descending induction with an explicit completed-ring inclusion computation (branches add, delta adds plus 1), and the reverse direction factors the normalization and kills the squishing alternative by contradiction. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: a systematic induction with clean bookkeeping hinges.
